title: Maximal bad quotient reduces projectivity to a reduced base
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a finite type flat homomorphism of commutative rings with $R$ Noetherian. Assume that $S\otimes_R K$ is a nonzero integral domain for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and every field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ (geometrically integral fibres), and that $S$ is not projective as an $R$-module. Then there is a proper radical ideal $I\subset R$ such that, writing $A=R/I$ and $B=S/IS$, the ring $A$ is nonzero, Noetherian and reduced (has no nonzero nilpotent elements), the map $A\to B$ is finite type and flat with geometrically integral fibres, $B$ is not projective over $A$, and $B/JB$ is projective over $A/J$ for every nonzero ideal $J\subseteq A$. Here radical means $x^n\in I$ for some $n\ge1$ implies $x\in I$. The notions of Noetherian, finite type, flat, projective, residue field and tensor product are as in [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], [def-weil-residue-field] and [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

proof.text: For any ideal $H\subseteq R$, the quotient $S/HS$ is flat over $R/H$. Indeed, for an injective $R/H$-linear map $U\to V$, regard it as an injective $R$-linear map. Flatness of $S$ makes $U\otimes_RS\to V\otimes_RS$ injective [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring], including its naturality, identifies this with $U\otimes_{R/H}(S/HS)\to V\otimes_{R/H}(S/HS)$. This is precisely flatness over $R/H$. Moreover, images of any finite set of $R$-algebra generators of $S$ generate $S/HS$ over $R/H$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, first proof paragraph: maximal bad ideal and radical reduction, including preservation under quotient base change

proof.text: Let $\Phi=\{H\subseteq R\mid S/HS\text{ is not projective over }R/H\}$. It contains $(0)$ by hypothesis, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-ideal-set-maximal] supplies a maximal member $I$. It is proper: for $H=R$, both quotients are zero, and the zero module is projective since every map out of it lifts uniquely along any surjection [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Thus $S/IS$ is not projective, while $S/HS$ is projective over $R/H$ for every $H\supsetneq I$.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, first proof paragraph: maximal bad ideal and radical reduction, including preservation under quotient base change

proof.text: Put $L=\sqrt I$. The ideal $L$ is finitely generated, say by $x_1,\ldots,x_t$, because $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Choose $n_i\geq1$ with $x_i^{n_i}\in I$ and set $N=1+\sum_i(n_i-1)$. Every degree-$N$ monomial in these generators has some exponent at least $n_i$, so $L^N\subseteq I$; if $t=0$, this reads $L^1=0\subseteq I$. Consequently $L/I$ is nilpotent in $R/I$. If $I\ne L$, maximality gives projectivity of $S/LS$ over $R/L$. Apply [lem-trf-local-nilpotent-projective-flat-lift] with ring $R/I$, ideal $L/I$, and module $S/IS$, flat by step 1. Its reduction is $S/LS$, since the kernel of $S/IS\to S/LS$ is $LS/IS=(L/I)(S/IS)$, and $(R/I)/(L/I)=R/L$. The lemma makes $S/IS$ projective, contradicting step 2. Hence $I=L$ is radical.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, first proof paragraph: maximal bad ideal and radical reduction, including preservation under quotient base change

proof.text: Set $A=R/I$ and $B=S/IS$. Properness of $I$ gives $1_A\ne0$. For an ideal $J$ of $A$, its inverse image $H$ in $R$ is finitely generated; images of generators of $H$ generate $J$. Thus $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. If $(r+I)^n=0$ with $n\geq1$, radicality gives $r\in I$, so $A$ is reduced. Step 1 supplies finite type and flatness of $A\to B$. For a nonzero ideal $J$ of $A$, its inverse image $H$ strictly contains $I$. The maps $(r+I)+J\mapsto r+H$ and $(s+IS)+JB\mapsto s+HS$ give compatible ring and module isomorphisms $A/J\cong R/H$ and $B/JB\cong S/HS$. The latter is projective over the former by step 2; the lifting-along-surjections characterization [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] transports this property through the displayed isomorphisms. This also covers $J=A$, where both quotient objects are zero.

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, first proof paragraph: maximal bad ideal and radical reduction, including preservation under quotient base change

proof.text: Finally let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime of $A$ and let $\mathfrak p$ be its inverse image in $R$. Then $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, and $A/\mathfrak q=R/\mathfrak p$ by $r+I\mapsto r+\mathfrak p$. Localizing this domain at all nonzero elements identifies the residue fields $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: both are fractions $\bar r/\bar t$ with $t\notin\mathfrak p$, with exactly the same equality relation. Equivalently these are the quotients of the corresponding local rings by their maximal ideals [def-weil-residue-field]. For any field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] with $H=I$, $M=S$ and quotient-ring module $K$ identifies $K\otimes_RS$ with $K\otimes_AB$ by $k\otimes s\mapsto k\otimes(s+IS)$. Swapping tensor factors on both sides, $u\otimes v\mapsto v\otimes u$, gives a ring isomorphism $S\otimes_RK\cong B\otimes_AK$ (multiplication agrees on pure tensors). The first ring is a nonzero integral domain by the original fibre hypothesis at $\mathfrak p$, so the second is too. This proves all required fibre conditions.
